title: Benefit, detriment, nominal price, and motives
shortTitle: Benefit, detriment, nominal price, and motives
summary: The notes refine the Hamer analysis through several different questions.
notes: First identify the conduct or return promise sought in exchange. Then separate its legal sufficiency from whether the values are equivalent. A stated nominal sum and a sham recital raise a genuineness issue rather than simply a pricing issue. Other motives can coexist with reciprocal inducement. The shorter family and research examples vary these elements to prevent reliance on one slogan.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 58–61. Open assigned page 58.
